facts.text: On this date in 1571, the Battle of Lepanto ended Ottoman naval dominance in the Mediterranean — fought by over 400 ships, it remains the largest galley battle in history.
On this date in 1985, the Achille Lauro hijacking began. The ship was seized in the Mediterranean by four Palestinian militants, exposing how unprepared the world was for maritime terrorism.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire United States west of the Mississippi River.
Vatican City generates more revenue per square meter than any nation on Earth — its museums alone draw over 6 million visitors a year into 0.17 square miles.
Norway owns more electric vehicles per capita than any other country, yet remains one of the world's largest oil exporters — it simply keeps the fossil fuels for everyone else.
On this date in 1987, the Dow had just peaked above 2,700 — within two weeks it would lose 22% in a single day, the largest one-day crash in market history.
On October 7, 1929, investors were still buying the dip. The Great Crash was still three weeks away, and Wall Street analysts were publicly calling the bull market intact.
The NYSE's famously chaotic trading floor now executes less than 10% of US equity volume. Most trades happen in windowless data centers in New Jersey.
Berkshire Hathaway's original business was a failing textile mill. Buffett later called buying it the worst investment of his life — it cost him roughly $200 billion in opportunity losses.
The Swiss franc is so trusted that during the 2011 eurozone crisis, Switzerland had to peg its currency to the euro to stop it from appreciating into economic ruin.
On this date in 1958, NASA officially opened for business. The agency was created in direct response to Sputnik's launch exactly one year prior, born from pure Cold War panic.
On this date in 2001, anthrax-laced letters began killing people in the US. The spores used were later traced to a US Army biodefense lab — the attack came from inside the building.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body replaces the lining of your small intestine every two to four days. The organ most responsible for keeping you alive is also one of the fastest self-destructing things in nature.
Light from the Sun takes eight minutes to reach Earth, but took roughly 100,000 years to fight its way from the Sun's core to its surface before that journey even began.
On this day in 1571, the Battle of Lepanto ended Ottoman naval dominance in the Mediterranean — fought the same year Shakespeare turned seven.
Nietzsche finished *Thus Spoke Zarathustra* in 1883, closer in time to the Battle of Waterloo than to today.
On this day in 1985, the Achille Lauro hijacking began. The ship's passenger list included more survivors of WWII than victims of the hijacking itself.
The Library of Alexandria was already ancient history by the time the Roman Colosseum was built — Romans lived closer to us than they did to the pyramids' construction.
Oxford University began teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. When Montezuma I took power in 1440, Oxford had been running for over three centuries.
Saudade (Portuguese): a melancholic longing for something beloved and gone. Linguists consider it untranslatable — a whole emotional climate compressed into eight letters.
Hiraeth (Welsh): homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or never had. The word carries grief, nostalgia, and yearning simultaneously, with no English equivalent.
On this date in 1571, the Battle of Lepanto was fought — and Miguel de Cervantes called it 'the most noble occasion that past or present ages have seen.' He lost use of his left hand there.
Meraki (Greek): the soul poured into your work. When a craftsman loses himself in what he's making, Greeks have a single word for that dissolving of self into effort.
On this date in 1849, Edgar Allan Poe died — his final word, reportedly, was 'Reynolds,' a name nobody has ever satisfactorily explained.

On this date in 2021, the SEC rejected VanEck's Bitcoin ETF application for the fourth time — citing manipulation concerns in spot markets. The approval finally came in January 2024, after 11 years of industry attempts.
On this date in 2013, Silk Road was seized by the FBI. The 144,000 BTC confiscated — then worth ~$28M — were later auctioned by the U.S. Marshals Service, partly to Tim Draper.

Bitcoin's timelock opcode OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY was only added in 2015 via BIP 65. Before it existed, time-locked transactions were technically possible but required trusting miners not to include them early.
Ethereum's gas limit is set by miners — now validators — not by protocol hard-code. Every block, the proposer can move it 1/1024th up or down, making block capacity a continuous on-chain negotiation.
The largest single Bitcoin transaction by value occurred in November 2011: 500,000 BTC moved in one transfer. At 2024 peak prices, that single UTXO represented over $47 billion in notional value.

On this date in 1950, Alan Turing's 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' was published in Mind — introducing the imitation game 76 years before the models it described became mundane infrastructure.

On this date in 2015, Google announced it had begun using RankBrain, a machine-learned ranking signal, in all search queries — the first time a learned system had been trusted with 100% of Google's core product.

GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 gigawatt-hours of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average US households, spent to produce a single set of weights.

The 2017 Transformer paper ('Attention Is All You Need') was rejected from a top venue before publication. Its eight authors have since collectively accumulated citation counts exceeding 200,000 from that single paper.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — essentially the entire known protein universe — in roughly 18 months. Experimental biology had accumulated ~170,000 structures across the prior six decades.
